headline: Agreed to repeal a blanket transportation impact fee waiver and to adjust transportation and recreation impact fees.
summary: The committee discussed impact fee waivers, inflation adjustments since 2014, and possible fees for the new Police Station and Concord School District Middle School. The committee agreed to proceed with fee adjustments for FY2027 through FY2029 and to research a debt service fee for those two projects.
decisions: Approved the minutes of April 8, 2026 unanimously.
Recommended amendments to the Impact Fee Ordinance to remove the blanket waiver and add a waiver process with specific criteria.
Consensus to repeal the automatic transportation impact fee waiver for nonresidential development and to craft a new waiver provision with specific criteria.
Consensus to adjust transportation and recreation impact fees with 5% catch-up plus inflation, capped at 8% in FY2027 and FY2028, and automatic inflation increases starting in FY2029.
Consensus to research the potential cost of an impact fee to support debt service for the new Police Station and Concord School District Middle School.

AD-HOC IMPACT FEE REVIEW COMMITTEE 
Minutes 
September 1, 2026 @ 4:00PM 
City Hall Large 2nd Floor Conference Room 
41 Green Street, Concord NH 03301 
 
Attendees: 
 Byron Champlin, Mayor 
 Judith Kurtz, At-Large City Councilor 
 Brent Todd, Ward 1 City Councilor 
 Jeff Foote, Ward 10 City Councilor 
 Bill Norton, Resident, representative of the Greater Concord Chamber of Commerce  
 Chuck Gilboy, guest / member of the Economic Development Advisory Committee 
 
Public: 
 None 
 
Staff: 
 Matt Walsh, Deputy City Manager, Development 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:00PM   
 
1. Nonpublic Session with Legal Counsel in accordance with RSA 91-A:2, I (b) 
Councilor Todd moved to enter nonpublic session for attorney client meeting with the City Solicitor in 
accordance with RSA 91-A:2, I (b). Mayor Champlin seconded.  The motion carried unanimously.  The 
session began at 5:01PM and ended at 5:21PM. 
 
2. Minutes of April 8, 2026 
Bill Norton moved to approve the minutes as presented.  Councilor Kurtz seconded.  The motion carried 
unanimously. 
 
3. Recap of Economic Development Advisory Committee Input from April 28, 2026 
Mayor Champlin, Chuck Gilboy, Judith Kurtz, Jeff Foote, and Matt Walsh provided a synopsis of the 
Economic Development Advisory Committee’s discussion of impact fees on April 28, 2026. (All had 
attended the EDAC meeting). It was noted that several members of EDAC had no prior knowledge or 
understanding of impact fees, thus a significant amount of education and orientation was required.  Some 
members of EDAC were not supportive of the City assessing impact fees to new development, others were 
neutral or did not take a position on the issue. 
 
  
 
CITY OF CONCORD 
New Hampshire’s Main Street™ 
41 Green Street, Concord NH 03301 
(603) 225-8570

4. Work Session 
Councilor Todd kicked off a work session discussion with the Ad-Hoc Committee.  He provided a recap of 
the Planning Board’s original recommendations to City Council to adjust transportation and recreation fees 
for inflation; noting that fees had not been adjusted since 2014.  He also provided a brief synopsis of 
previous discussions and ideas discussed by the Ad-Hoc Committee, which were summarized in a 
memorandum included in the agenda packet. 
 
Discussion ensued.   
 
The Ad-Hoc Committee discussed repeal of the blanket transportation impact fee waiver for nonresidential 
development.  It was the consensus of the Committee to recommend amendments to the Impact Fee 
Ordinance to remove the blanket waiver and replace with alternative waiver process – which would be 
available to nonresidential and residential development projects - with specific criteria for evaluating and 
granting waivers. 
 
Discussion also ensured about adjustments for inflation. It was noted the no rate increases for inflation had 
occurred since 2014. Various proposals were made for potential rate increases to adjust for past inflation, as 
well as such adjustments in the future. Proposals included amending the Impact Fee Ordinance so that 
annual adjustments for inflation would become automatic. 
 
Additional discussion ensued regarding potential enactment of impact fees to support the new Police Station 
and Concord School District Middle School Projects.  It was noted that both are creating capacity to serve 
future development, and thus potentially eligible for impact fees to support associated debt service as 
authorized by NH State Law RSA 674:21.  The Committee discussed ways impact fees could support these 
projects, such as partially supporting future debt service payments on that portion of these projects that 
creates capacity to serve future growth.   
 
After additional discussion, it was the consensus of the Ad-Hoc Committee to proceed as follows: 
 
a. Repeal the automatic waiver for transportation impact fees for nonresidential development 
b. Craft a new waiver provision with specific criteria whereby applicants may apply for waivers for 
nonresidential and residential development projects.  Criteria shall include, but not be limited to, 
demonstrating financial need to make the project economically viable. Other potential waiver criteria 
might include elimination of blight, or fostering goals set forth in the Master Plan (such as 
redevelopment of the opportunity corridor).   
c. Adjust transportation and recreation impact fees as follows: 
a. FY2027: 5% catch up to account for lack of inflationary increase during 2014-2026, plus 
actual inflation per construction cost indexes set forth within the Impact Fee Ordinance, with 
a maximum not to exceed combined total increase of 8% in FY 2027. 
b. FY2028: 5% catch up to account for lack of inflationary increase during 2014-2026, plus 
actual inflation per construction cost indexes set forth within the Impact Fee Ordinance, with 
a maximum not to exceed combined total increase of 8% in FY 2028. 
c. FY2029 and beyond: Inflation per construction cost indexes set forth within the Impact Fee 
Ordinance, and that annual inflationary increases become automatic starting in FY2029. 
d. Research the potential cost to develop an impact fee to support debt service costs for the new Police 
Station and Concord School District Middle School. 
 
The Committee will meet on October 28th at 5:00PM to review a draft ordinance prepared by Staff, as well 
as result of research into potential cost of engaging a consultant for potential impact fees associated with the 
new Police Station and Middle School projects.

5. Other Business  
None. 
 
6. Adjourn  
The meeting adjourned at 6:45PM. 
 
Respectfully Submitted; 
 
 
Matthew R. Walsh 
Deputy City Manager – Development
